Synopsis:
    A Norwegian court ordered the seizure of the Russian cruise/supply vessel Professor Molchanov in Svalbard, acting on behalf of Ukrainian energy company Naftogaz, which is enforcing a $4.22bn arbitration award stemming from Russia's 2014 annexation of Crimea. The ship served Russian settlements on the archipelago. Norway pledges humanitarian assistance to stranded Russians while Moscow accuses Oslo of piracy and has announced an appeal. The incident adds friction to Norway-Russia Arctic relations but remains primarily a legal/diplomatic dispute at this stage.

Relevance: NO — The article centres on a legal/diplomatic maritime dispute in the Arctic. The Naftogaz compensation claim relates to Crimea-era asset seizures, not to gas or power supply chains directly.
